articles.title: 7 Miles Out review – Carol Morley’s funny-poignant self-portrait of teenage kicks in Stockport
articles.summary: A daring, rich and funny study of the ordeal of having to invent and reinvent your own teenage sense of self amid confounding changes. Carol Morley’s self-portrait of the artist as a young woman is rich, tender and terribly funny and sad: a study in the chaos of being young and a triptych of…
body: 7 Miles Out is based on Morley’s autobiographical novel of the same title, the once-upon-a-time-in-Stockport story of Ann, played with charm and zing by Lucy Halliday, and as a sweetly innocent young girl by Amelie Hughes. Young Ann pretends to be making a radio programme with her cassette recorder the way so many did in the 1970s, and hero-worships her would-be rock journalist elder brother Scott (Kasper Hilton-Hille) – based on Morley’s brother Paul – who is already plugged into the burgeoning post-punk and new wave scene.

Ann’s mum Bryn, wonderfully played by Gemma Whelan, is capable and good-humoured in a no-nonsense sort of way, but later to be beset with anger and mercurial depression. She has however found something to smile about now in the news that her husband and Ann’s dad Ronald, played by Aidan Gillen, has found a prestigious new job in Manchester – seven miles out. So to get to work, he has apparently been supplied with a handsome, though not brand-new car.
points: A daring, rich and funny study of the ordeal of having to invent and reinvent your own teenage sense of self amid confounding changes.

articles.title: Gene Schwam, Veteran Hollywood Publicist to Elvis Presley, Julie Andrews and More, Dies at 96
articles.summary: Veteran Hollywood publicist Gene Schwam, who represented top talent including Elvis Presley, Blake Edwards, Julie Andrews, Barbara Eden and Lenny Bruce, died Friday in Los Angeles after a brief illness. He was 96.
body: Schwam co-founded Hanson & Schwam Public Relations with Adeline Hanson in 1955, establishing an independent publicity agency that would endure for decades.
Clients included Nancy Wilson and Lou Rawls, as well as the famous Coconut Grove nightclub, which helped the agency foster relationships with numerous entertainers.

His colorful representation (and intentional misreputation) of Presley in 1957 was covered in Variety at the time of the release of Baz Luhrmann’s “Elvis” in 2022. Schwam’s longtime relationship with Edwards extended beyond the professional. He was a friend as well as a publicist to the legendary director of such classics as “Breakfast at Tiffany’s,” “10,” and“Victor/Victoria.”

Edwards’ character of the neurotic publicist in his film “S.O.B.” was based on Schwam. That friendship reflected something fundamental about Schwam’s approach: he was known for his passionate engagement and resourceful guidance of his clients’ careers.

articles.title: How NBC Brought Live Musicals Back to Television
articles.summary: In 2011, NBC was in a rough shape. The network had struggled in the waning years under General Electric’s ownership. In January 2011, Comcast became the majority shareholder, and with it came a new leadership regime for NBC Entertainment, led by industry veteran Bob Greenblatt.
body: Nobody — not even Greenblatt, Zadan or Meron — quite knew what NBC had until the opening moments of the production on Dec. 5, 2013. Within minutes, fans ranging from Tina Fey to Cameron Diaz to everyday people who love tuners were chiming in on Twitter with posts noting the joy of singing along with the beloved Rodgers and Hammerstein standard.
Greenblatt credits the late producer Zadan and his longtime partner Meron for picking “Sound of Music” as the one to roll the dice on.

“They thought it could bring in a huge audience since it’s beloved by adults and children and is constantly being produced all over the world,” Greenblatt says. “We had no idea how to even produce a live musical or how we could market it since it there hadn’t been anything like it in decades. But everyone at the network got excited about it and came together to turn it into a powerhouse.”

articles.title: Harry Styles Debuts Unreleased Song He Wrote in Memory of Liam Payne, ‘What Is Enough,’ on Second Anniversary of Ex-Bandmate’s Death
articles.summary: The mood was typically celebratory at Harry Styles’ residency show at New York’s Madison Square Garden Friday night, but Harry Styles was not about to let the second anniversary of the death of former One Direction bandmate Liam Payne go unremarked upon — or, to the shock of fans, unsung about.
body: Styles backed into the song with a preamble that at first seemed just to be a “drive safely”-type goodnight message, before it turned out to be much more than that. “I hope you keep looking after each other, and please get home safety,” he said. “Tell a stranger you love ’em; tell your friends that you love ’em.”
Following the surprising premiere, Styles returned to the show’s regularly scheduled programming, rounding out the encore with “Sign of the Times” and “Aperture.”

articles.title: Miley Cyrus Tears Up While Honoring Dolly Parton During Hollywood Bowl Show: ‘Nothing In This Life Could Ever Tear Us Apart’
articles.summary: Miley Cyrus paid tribute to her late godmother and country icon Dolly Parton onstage at the Hollywood Bowl Friday as she performed her first major show in years. The “Bass Persuades” singer began by sharing memories with Parton, telling the audience she was partly inspired to play the venue because…
body: Parton died Aug. 25 after a “brief battle” with cancer. The family’s official obituary said, “A rhinestone life that shone bright enough for the world to see, Dolly will forever stand as an inspiration not only through her timeless music and prolific songwriting, but also her wit, warmth, and kindness that made us all feel like family. Dolly Parton’s legacy is one of love, compassion, and resilience. With a seven-decade career, she inspired multiple generations of artists and fans with her music and an unwavering commitment to making the world a better place. Her songs will continue to resonate with people of all ages, and her philanthropic work will have a lasting impact.”

Following her death, Cyrus s hared an emotional tribute to Instagram. “The feeling of losing my Aunt Dolly is beyond what feels right to share. Our most sacred moments were private and they’ll stay there behind the stage, beneath the glamour & between our hearts,” Cyrus wrote. “What I KNOW is Dolly would want me to feel it, write a song about it, and then continue on and be strong. I have an angel by my side. I always have. One of our last conversations was about music and metamorphosis.”

articles.title: ‘You can’t make this stuff up’: why we remain fascinated by Elizabeth Holmes
articles.summary: The entrepreneur turned fraudster is the subject of an Oscar-tipped new documentary that takes an unusual look at her strange legacy. David Agus’s first encounter with Elizabeth Holmes at a health conference came as a shock. The Holmes he met in the green room was personable and pleasant.
body: “The accent changed: this deep voice, very serious,” Agus, a medical oncologist, recalls by phone from Los Angeles. “It was as if I had met a person and then interviewed a separate person. That transition from the green room to the stage – I had never experienced something like that before.”

Holmes is not like you or me. She was still a teenager when she founded Theranos, touting technology capable of performing medical tests using only a few drops of blood. She cultivated a distinctive persona: blond hair, an unblinking gaze, a husky voice and a black turtleneck worn in homage to Apple co-founder Steve Jobs.

Holmes mesmerised investors and board members including Rupert Murdoch, Larry Ellison, Carlos Slim and former secretaries of state Henry Kissinger and George Shultz. She became America’s youngest self-made female billionaire. But it was all an illusion, a confidence trick built on a scam. Holmes’s shining career ended in disgrace and imprisonment.

articles.title: Off Campus star collaboration 'gave me chills', says Babydoll singer
articles.summary: Jamie Miller hopes he's "doing Wales proud" as his viral hit narrowly misses out on UK number one.
body: The singer behind the TikTok viral hit Babydoll says collaborating with an Off Campus star was "mind-boggling".
Jamie Miller, who is originally from Pontprennau in Cardiff, was close to calling it quits on his music career at the start of 2026, deciding it was his "last chance", financially and emotionally.

But over the summer everything changed when Babydoll caught the attention of people on social media, leading to a viral dance, his first UK top 10 single, and reaching number one in the US iTunes pop chart.
When Miller saw a comment from actor Antonio Cipriano, saying he "needed this song", he sent him a message suggesting he feature on a recording – then "panicked" and added "haha, joking".

articles.title: ‘American Horror Story’ Actor Orlando Jones on Taking Over Lance Reddick’s Role and His Season 13 Prediction: “Somebody Gonna Die!”
articles.summary: The veteran actor speaks with The Hollywood Reporter about his debut as Papa Legba in the Ryan Murphy universe, the witches' fight against Satan and the "magical" experience of sharing the screen with Jessica Lange and the returning Coven cast.
body: Among the many characters returning to American Horror Story: 13 is Papa Legba, with Orlando Jones taking over the role originally introduced in the horror anthology series’ third season, Coven, and season eight, Apocalypse, played by Lance Reddick, who died in 2023.

But this time, Papa is in an unusual position: he becomes the Coven’s ally and key source of information about Satan’s (aka Mr. Nas, played by Paul Anthony Kelly ) plan, a greater demonic threat, and how they can stop him to prevent the end of the world. The plan in question: Satan plans to leave Earth once his son, revealed to be Ben (Joey Pollari), claims his throne. So the witches must find the son to stop him from accepting the role. However, Ben finds them first, as episode 10 ends with Ben arriving at the Coven’s doorstep.

Below, Jones breaks down whether Papa can be trusted, the behind-the-scenes prosthetics, makeup and hair process behind his transformation, how “magical” it is to be set with the Coven women, especially with Jessica Lange ‘s return, his thoughts on the witches’ fate and more.

articles.title: How A New Star Trek Documentary Wants To Redefine What It Means To Be A Fan [Exclusive]
articles.summary: We spoke with the director of The Sixty-Year Mission, which is playing in Regal theaters now, about Star Trek fandom and what he wanted to do with his new doc.
body: As a franchise, "Star Trek" knows a thing or two about what it means to cast an immensely large shadow, and all the challenges that can come from that. For the longest time, the cast of "The Original Series" simply defined what "Trek" was and nothing could possibly hope to overtake the likes of William Shatner's Captain Kirk, Leonard Nimoy's Spock, and DeForest Kelley's Bones — until "The Next Generation" came around, that is, and proved that fans could come to accept a whole new captain and a whole new crew of intrepid explorers. On the other hand, there are certain aspects of the property that have become more famous for their pop-culture parodies and meme potential than anything else.

"I think, for better or worse, the brilliant 'Saturday Night Live' skit 'Get A Life' that Shatner did has defined what 'Star Trek' fans are to a generation. And I think I was trying to recapture the conversation and say 'Star Trek' is more than 'Get a Life.' 'Star Trek' is about celebrating these values of hope and optimism and embracing science and demonizing xenophobia and all these things that 'Star Trek' gave us, and bringing that back into the conversation."

articles.title: ‘Simpsons’ Bosses Tease How They Want Show to Go Out at THR’s Most Powerful People in Animation Breakfast
articles.summary: Matt Groening and Matt Selman sat down for a keynote conversation at the event, which also featured a chat with 'Tangles' stars Abbi Jacobson and Samira Wiley.
body: Tied to its inaugural Animation Power List, The Hollywood Reporter hosted its first Most Powerful People in Animation breakfast on Friday, in a toast to both the legends and the newcomers.

Groening and Selman also touched on the show’s uncanny ability for predictions — Groening darkly teased, “We predict that live executions will be live streamed in the future … but to take the edge off, we’re going to ask animators to add wacky sound effects: gong and zap and maybe sad trombones” — and the upcoming Simpsons Movie 2, arriving 20 years after the first film.

“We still haven’t recovered from the first movie, basically,” Groening explained of the long gap between films. “The first time we did the first movie, it was the same people, the same number of animators and the same writers, and so it was exhausting. It was too hard. But finally, we have recovered enough that we no longer remember how hard it was.”

The pair also weighed in on the future of The Simpsons, with Selman noting, “I would love to not cling to the show forever and let fresh people keep it amazing forever. I hope the show goes on forever, but I don’t need to be the guy forever, and I had a good run.”

articles.title: Patrick Brammall Is Poised to Join the Ranks of Australia’s Great Exports
articles.summary: With 'Colin From Accounts' now behind him, the actor-writer the collaboration with his wife became a sleeper hit, upping his game with roles in 'The Devil Wears Prada 2' and 'Last Seen' and auditioning with his hands tied.
body: Brammall breaks into a few bits over our early October conversation, one where he covers the significance of Colin From Accounts, his daughter’s disinterest in the fact that he voices a character on Bluey and how he still has no idea what was really going on with his character on the bonkers Paramount+ supernatural drama Evil.

You’ve worked a lot in Australia and now a lot in the U.S. as well. I suspect that there are many aspects of television that are done differently. How, in you speaking to like studios and platforms, can you compare the response to pitching a show that starts with a dog getting hit by a car?

Australia and the U.K. didn’t have a problem with it. That’s funny. These two strangers meet at an intersection, she flashes her nipple, he gets distracted, he hits a dog. It’s hilarious. In America… not so hilarious. There’s even a website, doesthedogdie.com. So in when we were pitching it over here, we had to start with, “The dog’s fine and he’s very well cared for.” And you do meet his previous owner at the end of the first season. That guy was an asshole. Colin’s got a much happier life.
